question.problem: Consider the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x+4y \\ -x+2y\end{aligned}].$ Find $\,\text{Ker}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
Finding the kernel of $\,T\,$ is equivalent to finding the null space of the standard matrix of $\,T.$

For the given linear transformation, the standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].$

Setting $x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],$ we then need to solve the equation $Tx=0.$ First, we reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$ and $y.$ From the second equation, we obtain $y=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we have $x=0.$ 

Therefore, the kernel of the linear transformation $T$ is $\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\}.$
